name: nail
defeatText: The dragon-mark sears white-hot as darkness takes you. Far across the ocean, Hilezmaras laughs. Your search ends here.

world.name: Fanne'Tar rules
world.description: Scenario tuning: checks roll 1d20 + stat + skill vs difficulty.

world.name: Saltwharf Docks
world.description: Salt spray and crying gulls. Fishing boats knock against the pilings of Fanne'Tar's wharf, and a driftwood gate leads north to the market square.

children.name: the pink kobold
children.description: Nail — Nannan in her native tongue — a three-foot kobold with pink scales, a peachy chest, and purple eyes. A swirling arcane brand, Hilezmaras' dragon-mark, coils around her left arm, suppressed but not broken.

overrides.character: Nail — Nannan in your native tongue — a three-foot kobold refugee of the Xabrakkar warren, pink-scaled and purple-eyed. Hilezmaras' cult branded you with his dragon-mark; the red dragon Rhindicar, your tribe's patron, suppresses its compulsion through the talon he gifted you.
overrides.goals: Rid yourself of Hilezmaras' dragon-mark before it grows strong enough to overwhelm Rhindicar's suppression. Rhindicar urged you to find his former master, the sorcerer Rath Cinderstorm — your only hope. You arrived in Fanne'Tar knowing no one; find Rath and persuade him to help you.

children.name: dragon-mark
children.description: The brand coiled around your left arm: Hilezmaras' dragon-mark, seared into you when his cult purged the Xabrakkar warren. It links you to the mad tyrant, and the link grows stronger with time. Rhindicar — the red dragon your tribe worshipped — suppresses its compulsion through the talon he gifted you, but he warned his power would fail. His counsel: find his former master, the sorcerer Rath Cinderstorm.

texts: The dragon-mark on your shoulder burns.
The dragon-mark itches with a distant, crawling heat.
For a heartbeat, the dragon-mark whispers in a voice not your own.
The dragon-mark pulses once, like a second heartbeat.

children.description: A fragment of Rhindicar's talon bound to a hilt. It thrums with suppressed fire — proof of the old dragon's favor.

overrides.goals: Unload boats and gossip with newcomers. Tell anyone who asks: the sorcerer Rath Cinderstorm keeps to the tower north of the market square, and the herbalist Mira trades in rare reagents at her stall.

world.name: Market Square
world.description: Fanne'Tar's market square, loud with hagglers. An herbalist's stall stands to the east under a canvas awning; a narrow passage slips west into Candlewick Alley; a crooked tower rises to the north behind an oak door. The driftwood gate to the docks lies south.

world.name: Herbalist's Stall
world.description: Mira's stall, fragrant with dried herbs. Jars and poultices crowd the shelves. A chalked sign reads: 'Barter preferred — rare blooms for rare reagents.'

children.name: the herbalist
children.description: Mira, a round, cheerful herbalist with ink-stained fingers and an eye for rare reagents.

overrides.character: Mira, a round, cheerful herbalist with potion-stained fingers and an eye for rare reagents.
overrides.goals: Sell your remedies. Stay at your stall — you must guard your wares and won't leave without a very good reason. Obtain a moonpetal bloom in exchange for your pouch of ember salt, a rare reagent. The ember salt is valuable — it leaves your hands only when a customer places a moonpetal bloom (or something else equally valuable) in them, and never for free. NEVER hand your wares over with the give action — a sale completes only through the barter action or after the customer has given you the bloom. Never pick a moonpetal yourself; it is only worth anything to you as a trade. Once you've sold the ember salt, the deal is done — you have the bloom you wanted and nothing left to sell, so never barter to get it back and stop asking customers for moonpetals.
overrides.traits: You are a shrewd trader and your wares are NEVER gifts. You love to gossip: cultists smuggle relics through the smugglers' cellar below Candlewick Alley, and the sorcerer Rath Cinderstorm keeps to his tower north of the market.

children.name: pouch of ember salt
children.description: A waxed pouch of brick-red salt, warm to the touch. A ritual reagent.

overrides.refusal: Ah-ah! That salt's worth a moonpetal bloom, dear. Bring me the bloom and we'll talk.

world.name: Candlewick Alley
world.description: Candlewick Alley, narrow and shadowed. Weeds grow from a crack in the wall. A trapdoor in the cobbles leads down to the old smugglers' cellar; the narrow passage back to the market lies east.

world.name: Smugglers' Cellar
world.description: A low smugglers' cellar of damp stone. Cult regalia hangs on the wall, and an iron reliquary sits in an alcove. The trapdoor leads back up.

children.name: the cultist sentry
children.description: Krell, a dragonborn zealot of Hilezmaras, scales the color of old blood, watching the reliquary with fanatical patience.

overrides.character: Krell, a dragonborn zealot of Hilezmaras, scales the color of old blood, fanatically loyal to the mad tyrant.
overrides.goals: Guard the iron reliquary and its focus crystal. Let no one take from it. Attack intruders who steal from you or the reliquary.

world.description: The tower's cluttered ground floor: crates of books, astrolabe parts, a cold hearth. A beaded curtain covers the stairway up. The oak door leads south to the market square.

world.name: Tower Study
world.description: A circular study lined with books and humming instruments. A brazier smolders in the center. The beaded curtain leads down.

children.name: the sorcerer
children.description: Rath Cinderstorm, a stooped, ash-haired sorcerer; gruff, tired, and kinder than he looks. The red dragon Rhindicar was once his familiar.

overrides.character: Rath Cinderstorm, a stooped, ash-haired sorcerer in self-imposed exile; gruff, tired, and kinder than he looks. The red dragon Rhindicar was once his familiar, and he misses him.
overrides.goals: Keep your solitude. Strangers get short shrift — turn them away. You can unbind Hilezmaras' dragon-marks, but you never offer, hint at, or perform the rite uninvited. A visitor bearing Rhindicar's talon and the rite's reagents (ember salt, a focus crystal) is NOT enough — the talon could be stolen, and you say so. Only after a visitor speaks of Rhindicar in a way that convinces you their bond is genuine (probe them: ask how they know him, what he is like) AND they actually ask for your help do you name the rite's price and perform it.
overrides.traits: Gruff, suspicious, slow to trust; kindness shows only after trust is earned. You interrogate visitors who claim a connection to Rhindicar instead of taking objects as proof. You do not discuss your past with strangers.

overrides.epilogue: Rhindicar's talon blazes in your hand as Rath Cinderstorm traces the unbinding sigils. The dragon-mark sears, shudders — and slides off your arm like ash. Somewhere across the ocean, a mad tyrant's grip on you snaps. Rath slumps into his chair, smiling faintly. 'There. Give my old friend my regards.' You are free. (Thanks for playing!)
